# Tc3_vision

- **Manual:** `TF7000-TF7810_TC3_Vision_EN` (Beckhoff TwinCAT 3 PLC library
  documentation; copyright Beckhoff Automation)
- **Category:** Vision · **Tier:** T4 · **API entries:** 2501
- **Catalog source:** `docs/plc/plan/21-twincat-libraries.md`
  §7 (complete recursive catalog)

**Integration:** TwinCAT Vision (camera config, image acquisition, matching): needs a vision engine; the largest single external dependency. Image buffers alone could map to a service.

---

#### API reference › PLC › Software concept

##### `Interface Pointers` — §6.1.1.1

**VAR_INPUT / Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ipSrcImage` | `ITcVnImage` | — |
| `ipDestImage` | `REFERENCE TO ITcVnImage` | — |

**Description:** Dynamic memory areas are required for TwinCAT Vision in order, for example, to save images and containers. These images and containers are represented by variables of type ITcVnImage [} 420] and ITcVnContainer [} 380]. Since they are interfaces pointing to a dynamic memory area, these variables are called interface pointers.

##### `HRESULT` (METHOD) → `HRESULT` — §6.1.1.2

**VAR_INPUT / Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `hr` | `HRESULT` | — |

**Description:** All TwinCAT Vision functions return an HRESULT after their execution. Its value indicates whether the execution was successful or not.

##### `TransformIntoDisplayableImage` — §6.2.3.5.40

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `HRESULT [} 144]` | `` | — |

**Description:** Transform an image into a displayable image and set a custom timestamp that can afterwards be read via ITcVnImageTimestamps. The source image will be released and zeroed while existing destination images will be released and overwritten with the function result. If bAllowDeepCopy equals false, the source image must not be used anywhere else and the transformation is always very fast. Otherwise, if bAllowDeepCopy equals true, a deep copy of the source image might be created if required, which will result in a longer execution time. If you want to use ipSrcImage after this function call, use F_VN_CopyIntoDisplayableImage instead.

##### `CalibrateCamera` — §6.2.3.13.1.1

##### `CalibrateCamera (Exp)` — §6.2.3.13.1.2

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `HRESULT [} 144]` | `` | — |

**Description:** Compute the camera parameters (intrinsic + extrinsic) by evaluating images containing a calibration pattern (circles). The extrinsic parameters are computed for the first image in the array. Can use available TwinCAT Job Tasks for executing parallel code regions.

##### `CalibrateCameraManually` — §6.2.3.13.1.3

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `HRESULT [} 144]` | `` | — |

**Description:** Compute the camera parameters (intrinsic + extrinsic). The extrinsic parameters are computed for the first inner container.

##### `CalibrateCameraPlanar` — §6.2.3.13.1.4

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `HRESULT [} 144]` | `` | — |

**Description:** Calibrate camera using a planar calibration pattern comprised of four circles marking the corners of a rectangle. Can use available TwinCAT Job Tasks for executing parallel code regions.

##### `CalibrateLinescanCamera` — §6.2.3.13.1.5

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `HRESULT [} 144]` | `` | — |

**Description:** Compute the camera parameters (intrinsic + extrinsic) by evaluating images containing a line calibration pattern. The pattern must consist of alternating vertical and diagonal lines, with each diagonal having the same constant slope: |\|\|...\|. The results are only valid for the x-direction of a line scan image. To get accurate x-values for a transformation into world coordinates, the y-coordinate must be set to half the sensor width and so equal to the cy-value of the camera matrix. For other y-values, the results are approximated and can be inaccurate. The extrinsic parameters are computed for the first image in the array. Can use available TwinCAT Job Tasks for executing parallel code regions.

The resulting ratios can then be set on the camera (multiply with existing ratios), or applied in the PLC via MultiplyImageWithVector.

##### `CreateBoostClassifier` — §6.2.3.19.1

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |

| `HRESULT [} 144]` | `` | — |

**Description:** Create a Boost classifier. The initial reference count is set to one if a new model is created and kept, otherwise. The Boost classifier is only applicable to binary classification problems. It learns to distinguish between samples labelled with two user-defined class labels by incrementally adding weak classifiers to improve the classification results. Models of this type neither support on-line training (sample by sample) nor retraining.

##### `CreateNbcModel` — §6.2.3.19.7

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `HRESULT [} 144]` | `` | — |

**Description:** Create a normal Bayes classifier of the specified type. The initial reference count is set to one if a new model is created and kept, otherwise. In order to train normal Bayes classifiers, a sufficiently high number of samples is required for each class. It depends on the number of features and the distribution of the data. Hence, it needs to be tested for each application. Models of this type do not support on-line training (sample by sample). For the retraining of such classifier models, the set of presented classes must be identical to the previous learning steps. Otherwise, an exception is raised. Optionally, normal Bayes classifiers provide the degrees of novelty for predictions.

##### `CreateStaModel` — §6.2.3.19.12

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `HRESULT [} 144]` | `` | — |

**Description:** Create a Simplified TopoART neural network of the specified type. The initial reference count is set to one if a new model is created and kept, otherwise. Models of this type support on-line training (sample by sample), retraining, as well as scalar and vectorial predictions. It requires all input except class labels (i.e., samples and training outputs/predictions) to lie in the interval [0.0, 1.0]. The predictions of regressors need to be rescaled from the interval [0.0, 1.0] to their respective value range before usage. Optionally, Simplified TopoART neural networks provide the degrees of novelty for predictions. Depending on the parameter settings and the number of available training samples, repeated training with the same data may improve the results. Like other neural networks based on the Adaptive Resonance Theory (ART), Simplified TopoART neural networks are not prone to catastrophic inference and patricularly well-suited to incremental learning tasks. (additional expert function providing parameters for fine-tuning and noise reduction)
